newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Peru's embassy in Guatemala gets bomb hoax.
newsitem.headline: Peru's embassy in Guatemala gets bomb hoax.

text.p: Explosives experts and special police searched Peru's Embassy in Guatemala City on Wednesday after what turned out to be a bomb hoax, the fire department said.

The telephoned threat came the morning after a military raid on the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima, Peru, freed 71 hostages held by Marxist rebels since Dec. 17. All 14 rebels died along with one hostage and two soldiers.

"We are sure there are not any explosives in the area," a fire department spokesman said on local station Radio Sonora after a rapid response police force and bomb disposal experts searched the embassy building.

Peruvian Ambassador Julio Florian said he would ask Guatemala's foreign office to boost security at the embassy. "We are asking for additional protection, which is a reasonable obligation at this time," he told reporters.

Florian said he was making the request in light of the bomb threat and a student protest on Tuesday night in which about 50 students threw rocks at the embassy, chanted "assassins, assassins," and covered walls with slogans denouncing Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori.

Guatemalan officials applauded the military operation that freed the hostages in Peru. Solicitor General Acisclo Valladares told reporters Fujimori had reacted in the only way possible against the "delinquent terrorists" and added: "The authority of the law is what can assure peace for the people."

But leaders of the left condemned Fujimori for abandoning negotiations with the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA), the group holding the hostages. "The measure adopted yesterday by the Peruvian government radicalizes the positions and removes the possibilities of solving social conflicts through negotiation," Arnoldo Noriega Perez of the Political Council of the Guatemalan National Revolutionary Unit (URNG), told Siglo XXI newspaper.
